#4193. Marathon may actually have a shot as Server Slam hits it big on Steam

Marathon's latest public open weekend has kicked off, and it looks like enough people have showed up to play it.

Things are officially looking better for Marathon. The game’s Server Slam, essentially an open beta that’s freely available everywhere, has kicked off. This is the last chance for anyone curious about Bungie’s next big game to play it before it officially goes on sale next week.

Considering how unpopular the game has been throughout its development, and judging by the feedback from earlier closed beta tests, the turnout for the Server Slam is definitely encouraging.

The Marathon Server Slam has been online for a little over 12 hours on Steam, PS5, and Xbox Series X/S. Only one of those platforms shares player numbers, of course, but it's enough to offer some visibility into how popular the test has been.

Immediately after servers went live, Marathon shot up the Steam most played charts. The game quickly achieved a peak of 143,621 concurrent players (via SteamDB), which is very respectable. Given that the Server Slam will be available for the entire weekend, there’s every chance the numbers will go up.

These figures are particularly encouraging when you look at Arc Raiders, the current top dog in the extraction shooter space, and the game that stole Marathon’s thunder last year when the two of them were being promoted by their publishers. Marathon, of course, got delayed out of 2025, which allowed Arc Raiders to launch first. It, of course, ended up proving that extraction shooters can be mainstream hits.

Like Marathon, Arc Raiders hosted its own server slam just a few days before its launch. That open test attracted 189,668 concurrent players at its peak, which is not that far off from Marathon’s so far.

Assuming positive word of mouth continues, more players are bound to jump in over the weekend and perhaps get Marathon to match or even exceed Arc Raiders’ record. At any rate, this is good news for beleaguered Bungie and points to what could be a big launch.

Marathon arrives March 5 on PC, PS5, and Xbox Series X/S.

#4191. Halo: Campaign Evolved Announces PvE Firefight Is Returning For Free Update

With the franchise undergoing some major structural changes and a new studio at the helm for its next entry, Halo: Campaign Evolved is still kicking with new content to keep players engaged with the experience. While it might not be the return of the classic PvP mode that helped make the original Halo: Combat Evolved so iconic, the free update coming this winter is still a fan-favorite addition.

While most of Campaign Evolved's updates so far have simply been free cosmetic DLC, it was announced on the official Halo account on X that the "classic PvE experience" with Firefight will be returning, letting players experience the remake as a 4-player co-op horde shooter.

While there is no exact release date just yet for when we can expect the mode to go live in Campaign Evolved, the free content update is slated to arrive later this Winter, with more details revealed at this year's Halo Fest running from December 12–13.

Fans lucky enough to attend the Halo Fest event taking place in Seattle, WA will also have a chance to go hands-on with the mode for the first time.

If you've never heard of Firefight before or need a refresher, the defense-based mode can be played either alone or in co-op, where you and your team will face off against waves of attacking enemies that get progressively more challenging as time goes on, often with new and unique gameplay modifiers.

Would the addition of multiplayer really replace the magic of the original?

Although there has been plenty of excitement over the addition, especially over the fact that Campaign Evolved is still getting gameplay content despite the mass layoffs from the studio, some fans have pointed out that the mode doesn't exactly come as a surprise since it has been added post-launch to several recent entries already.

Even if some players already expected it, the announcement has still been met with plenty of cheers from fans and curious players alike, which offers more incentives to tune in for this year's Halo Fest to see what new gameplay changes Halo: Campaign Evolved's take on Firefight has in store for players ahead of Halo's next rumored sequel.

We want to hear from you. Share your perspective in the comments below, and please keep the conversation respectful.

#4190. Bit Reactor Exposes Clone Supremacy in Star Wars: Zero Company

Michael Manning (He/Him) has been enamored with video games since he first played the Sonic Classic Collection as a child. With decades of experience in gaming and a full tour as a Gaming Journalist, Michael is ready to step up to the plate. From AAA to the smallest passion projects, his motto is that every piece of ar

For tactics titles, how you choose to build your squad says far more about you than any character creator ever could. With a genre so focused on how its myriad mechanics intertwine, it’s up to the developers to give every kind of player the tools they could want. Even so, stronger options will bleed through, building a toolset adored by the community.

Grand Theft Auto 6 is on everyone's radar, including the South Korean ratings board, which barely let it pass inspection.

In Star Wars: Zero Company’s case, developers Bit Reactor had some of the raddest sections of Star Wars’ mythos to pull on, tools they gladly toss straight to players. With that said, recently released community stats have showcased exactly how the player base liked to deal with the problems posed by the Infinite Coil: Total Clone Devastation.

Stat sheets like this one are always fun, showcasing how exactly the larger community picked their way through Zero Company and where they stumbled. For a black sheep like Zero Company, which came out of nowhere between other big-budget Star Wars titles, it swung far above its weight class, giving the larger gaming space tactics they haven’t played with since the last XCOM title.

Trick, the resident Clone in the playable roster, was by far the most popular pick, standing as the most deployed operator with a whopping 74.5% use case, followed by Cly the Mandalorian at only 55%. It’s clear that gaming fans still adore the Clone era of Star Wars, with Trick standing tall amidst his same-faced brothers.

Trick’s optional Bond with Hawks is almost the most popular in the game, really setting him up to be the fan favorite. It wasn’t just Operator stats explored, with the larger community whipping out over 226,056,072 battle droids, not counting elites or special variants.

With a genre so focused on how its myriad mechanics intertwine, it’s up to the developers to give every kind of player the tools they could want.

Standing high above the chaff, the Coil Enforcer beat the most players down, while Visser took his throne as the deadliest boss by far. He alone took down over 35,000 Operators, serving as a rather infamous difficulty spike. Through these foes, around 21% of the player base lost their first recruit, adding even greater stakes to the campaign’s end.

When it came to major choices, the community fell in line more often than not, with an overwhelming 97% hiring on Cly as soon as the opportunity presented itself. Hawks’ playstyle also seemed to coalesce for most, setting them up as a Heavy/Gunslinger DPS monster. With tactics like this, its no wonder the community tore through so many.

When it comes to games, Zero Company is doing wonders to keep Star Wars’ head above water after the hectic swirl of news surrounding Battlefront 3. Between it and Galactic Racer, fans are showing up for the smaller-scale Star Wars adventures, reminding the larger industry, as well as EA, that not every title needs to be some massive budget epic.

Star Wars as a setting has always benefitted from feeling truly lived in, and for an entire galaxy to exist, most days need to be occupied with smaller action. Pod Racing, tight tactical skirmishes, maybe some space wizards clashing behind the scenes. While the big releases are hotly anticipated, fans are more than willing to step into the shoes of smaller players.

Clones especially provide a really great niche for games, allowing players to hop right into a recognizable face without needing to give them crazy story significance. You can’t always play as a Skywalker, but you can always hop straight into the shoes of a Clone Trooper, even outside of their era. At the end of the day, every Star Wars game just needs to bring something new, and the tactics of Zero Company are perfect.

Discord is potentially enabling all kinds of couch co-op play, enabling direct control over users' games.

#4189. The Sims 4 is getting paid mods, and a new in-game currency to pay for them

The Sims 4 is about to launch a couple of major initiatives that may not exactly be what players have been looking for.

The Sims 4 has officially entered into its paid mods era. Developer Maxis announced The Sims Maker Program, and The Sims 4 Marketplace - two new destinations to publish, and discover new add-on content.

The two new features will arrive first on PC and Mac, starting March 17. PlayStation and Xbox players will receive them over the next couple of months, which is very much in line with how other franchises have rolled out their own paid mods systems.

The Maker Program is a way for community creators to get their work out there, and profit from it. The content they create will end up on the Marketplace, where other players can browse it, and pay for it if they want to use it in their game.

Created content will be available across all platforms. All previous packs The Sims 4 players should be familiar with will move to the Marketplace, too: once the feature launches, this is where you’re going to find Expansion Packs, Game Packs, Stuff Packs, Kits, and other official additions created by Maxis.

Alongside this, the game is also introducing a new virtual currency - Moola - which is what you’re going to use to purchase Maker Packs, as well as Sims 4 Kits in the Marketplace. A portion of your purchase will go to the creator (roughly 30%) of what you buy.

It is worth noting, however, that you’ll still be able to buy Expansion Packs, Game Packs, and Stuff Packs without having to purchase Moola, or go through the Marketplace. Kits are the only items that will no longer be available on the existing PC/console storefronts. Moola comes in the usual denominations you’ve seen a hundred items in other games’ in-game shops.

In order to start creating custom content and publishing it on the Marketplace, you’ll need to first be accepted into the program. Once that’s done, you’ll be able to directly publish your content on the Marketplace.

In the blog post announcing the new features, Maxis said that creators will have control over the price of their content, and how it's packaged. These are referred to as Maker Packs, which can include Create-a-Sim or Build/Buy items.

You can apply to become a Maker from March 5. Once accepted, you’ll also get access to the Maker Suite, which is what you’re going to use to test your work to ensure it runs smoothly on the different platforms, and eventually publish it.

#4188. Grand Theft Auto VI Will Run At 30 FPS On All Consoles, But PS5 Pro Will Feature 'Improved Clarity' And Ray-Traced Shadows

Grand Theft Auto VI launches next week on Thursday, November 19, and you can preload the game on your PlayStation 5 or Xbox Series X/S starting today, Rockstar Games has announced. The studio has also revealed what kind of visuals players can expect on their respective consoles, making clear that regardless of where you play, GTA VI targets 30 FPS gameplay.

"Grand Theft Auto VI has been fully developed from the ground up to provide the best possible experience for the current generation of consoles, targeting 30 frames per second while pushing both platforms to their absolute limits to bring the vast and rich world of Leonida to life – while maintaining the density and visual fidelity of all its environments and inhabitants," Rockstar writes in a blog post.

Rockstar Games also breaks down the different graphical settings available on PlayStation and Xbox consoles. On PS5 Pro, GTA VI will feature "improved clarity through PlayStation Spectral Super Resolution (PSSR) and ray-traced shadows only available on PlayStation 5 Pro." On PS5 and PS5 Pro, the game will include "high-fidelity haptic feedback" fully integrated into DualSense controllers and adjustable via accessibility settings, improved spatial rendering so all in-game sounds take full advantage of Tempest 3D audio, and improved load times, "making Grand Theft Auto VI play best on PlayStation 5 consoles."

On Xbox consoles, Rockstar doesn't dive into performance; instead, it focuses on Xbox Cloud Gaming on Xbox Series X/S and Xbox One consoles, noting this feature will use Xbox Series S graphics settings.

GTA VI will also fully support Remote Play on PlayStation and Xbox.

GTA VI launches November 19 on PS5 and Xbox Series X/S.

For more, check out the song "Pusher" from the game's original score, then check out the GTA VI launch trailer. After that, check out this exclusive story about how GTA VI features over 170 animal species and another about its tropical storms and hurricanes.

Where will you play GTA VI? Let us know in the comments below!

#4187. Update: You Can Preload Grand Theft Auto VI On PS5 and Xbox Today, And You Should Because It's Massive

Rockstar Games revealed last week that players can preload Grand Theft Auto VI on their console of choice the following week, and that time has arrived. The studio released a blog post today to announce that you can preload GTA VI on PlayStation 5, PlayStation 5 Pro, Xbox Series X, and Xbox Series S. If you're excited about the game, you will probably want to go ahead and do this because it will take up a whopping 212 GB of space on your drives – make the room now so you don't hit this roadblock next week when the game goes live on Thursday, November 19.

The blog post also details performance on PlayStation and Xbox consoles, and you can read more about what to expect here.

We're just over two weeks away from the launch of Grand Theft Auto VI, which recently graced the cover of Game Informer. Ahead of its November 19 launch, Rockstar Games has announced that digital preloading for GTA VI will begin next week on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X/S.

More specifically, preloading on Xbox Series X/S will begin Tuesday, November 10, at 12 a.m. GMT (4 p.m. PT/7 p.m. ET on November 9), and on PS5 at midnight local time in your time zone. Although Rockstar isn't producing physical discs of GTA VI, you can still buy a physical box at retail, which includes a download code for the game. The studio says, "Code-in-box versions for both consoles should be available from retailers beginning November 12."

The preload file will require 212 GB on your device, so make sure you have the space before you start the download. You can find more details about this process here.

Elsewhere in today's GTA VI news, Rockstar has revealed that on November 19, it will add an official printable GTA VI cover art poster and a map of Leonida as a free digital download to the game's official site. However, a double-sided physical version of this poster will be made available shortly after the launch of GTA VI from the Rockstar Store. It will only cost $0.99 on its own, or come free with any other purchase from the store.

GTA VI launches November 19 on PS5 and Xbox Series X/S.

For more, check out the song "Pusher" from the game's original score, then check out the GTA VI launch trailer. After that, check out this exclusive story about how GTA VI features over 170 animal species and another about how the game features tropical storms and hurricanes.

#4186. Our first look at Diablo 4's Warlock and the game's next season arrive in today's livestream - watch it here

Diablo 4's latest Developer Update is nearly upon us, and it's one plenty of the game's fans and players have been looking forward to.

Diablo 4’s next, long-awaited Developer Update finally airs today. This meaty livestream was first announced nearly a month ago, when Blizzard initially revealed that the game’s next class is the Warlock.

The Warlock’s initial unveiling, however, was incredibly brief, showing no gameplay. It also didn't explain how the class is going to fit within the existing roster. This all changes today.

Blizzard is bringing back its Developer Update livestream programme, which is the more structured, information-dense series of developer showcases. The focus of this one, of course, is going to mainly be on the Warlock class.

The Warlock is one of two classes coming to Diablo 4 with the upcoming Lord of Hatred expansion. The first, the Paladin, is already available in the game for anyone who pre-orders the expansion. The Warlock will instead arrive alongside the expansion on April 28.

The Developer Update will also include a first look at the game’s next season (Season 12), currently set for March 10. This mini season will only last until the expansion’s release, so it’s going to be interesting to see what it brings to the game.

You’ll be able to watch the showcase live at 11am PT, 2pm ET, 7pm GMT on Diablo 4’s official YouTube, Twitch, and Twitter channels. We’ve embedded the YouTube and Twitch players below for your convenience.

Among the topics the Developer Update will cover are the Killstreaks system, as well as Bloodstained items. As always, you can also expect a Q&A segment at the end of the show, and I imagine there’s going to be a few about the Warlock.

#4185. Don't Play Hell Let Loose On PS Plus Extra If You Claimed It Through Essential

Hell Let Loose was confirmed to be among November’s PS Plus Extra games on Tuesday and has already been added to the subscription service’s middle tier. However, you’ll want to double-check if it’s already in your library, and figure out how it got there, before you download it and dive in.

Team17’s first-person shooter drops you into World War 2 onto battlefields with 99 other players. Yes, it’s a war-based multiplayer game like Call of Duty, but it offers up a very different experience to most other games in the same genre. That’s why there will likely be a lot of you giving it a go now that it’s on Extra.

Every game coming to Essential, Extra, and Premium and the dates you'll be able to play them for free.

Hell Let Loose was actually an early example of a game that launched day one on PS Plus, all the way back in October 2021. It stands to reason that you may have forgotten about it, especially if you played it for a little while and then never went back, or if you’re the kind of person who claims every free game, even if you might never play them.

Therein lies the problem, as highlighted by PlayStation Lifestyle. If you previously claimed Hell Let Loose through Essential, forgot that you did that, and now claim the game again through Extra, the Extra license may override your Essential one. That means, if and when Hell Let Loose leaves Extra, you will lose access to the game, even though you technically should own the license if you claimed it in 2021.

If you previously bought the game, this isn’t an issue. It only seems to be a problem for games that were given away via Essential and then later added to Extra, with users not being told the game is already in their library before they download it through Extra. If it’s already too late, then when Hell Let Loose does eventually leave Extra, you can try to contact PlayStation to reinstate your Essential license, but that might not be possible. If you are planning on playing Hell Let Loose through Extra, just check you don’t already have it. You might have no memory of claiming it, but again, it was five years ago, and you may have just absentmindedly claimed every game that month and move on.

Lots of new stuff if you have PS Plus, but not nearly enough to get PlayStation back in people's good books.

#4184. Random: Yes, Young Link Is Still Quicker When He Rolls About In Ocarina's Remake

As many fans begin to wrap up their first play sessions of Zelda: Ocarina of Time on Switch 2, more attention is slowly shifting to the game's speedrunning community.

During the Zelda Direct, Mr. Aonuma noted how child Link's new "dash" ability had been introduced in the remake because many players in the original game would often roll from one point to another. While it is definitely a faster option than walking, it turns out rolling is still a slightly quicker way to get to your destination (at least as Young Link) in the remake.

Speedrunners have now time-trialled Young Link dashing and rolling across Hyrule on the Switch 2, and if you roll about, you should arrive at your location sooner. And hey, every second counts when it comes to speedrunning!

Zelda speedrunning channel 'Kethnaldo' took a closer look, and between running (dashing) and rolling, the real winner here is the technique referred to as "forward hop roll-cancelling", which in one demonstration sees the player run from Koriki Forest to Hyrule Castle and arrive at the castle roughly four seconds earlier than other methods.

"After you front hop, you can roll immediately and get rid of that end lag...so all you're doing is target forward hopping to get that insane momentum, rolling immediately to get rid of all of the end lagging, and then front hopping again as soon as possible to maximise that front hop speed, and you just chain them together as best as you can...you will mess up, but even with mess ups...it's about roughly four seconds faster than running."

So if you want to speed things up when you're on foot as Young Link, rolling is still recommended. And if you can nail the other technique, you'll be shaving quite a bit off the adventure. Of course, keep in mind, this isn't the original Zelda: Ocarina of Time, so there's always a chance Nintendo could make subtle or major adjustments to game mechanics in future game updates.

#4183. House House Discloses AI Use For 'Under 0.1%' Of Big Walk's Code Following IGF Voting Controversy

Big Walk developer House House has found itself at the center of a controversy over the upcoming Independent Games Festival on March 3, 2027, after a group of its jurors said they would not vote for any game that has used generative AI in any capacity. The jurors' statement does not name House House or Big Walk, but the studio eventually updated its FAQ to explain how it used generative AI for coding after IGF discussions. After vaguely posting on social media, those associated with IGF made clear that a sticking point in the voting process was Big Walk.

Former games journalist and game developer Austin Walker posted the IGF jurors' statement on Bluesky, explaining that voting has been difficult this year due to the "significant increase in the number of submitted games developed with generative AI tools."

"This has set off some fairly intense discussion and disagreement across the judge and jury pools, and at this point there is no universal consensus on what (if anything) is to be done," the statement reads. "The IGF has affirmed that we may cast our votes according to our own tastes and values. But we, as a contingent of IGF jurors, feel that this trend and the games embracing it deserve stronger pushback than a vote in silence."

The statement continues, explaining that not all jurors are on board with the blanket statement, citing reasons including "their ability to safely sign without professional blowback." It continues, "Above all: Our goal is to state solidarity with those who despair over the future of their art, their craft, and their industry – including those who have experimented with these tools, but who now believe they are not in our best interest."

The statement continues with the jurors' beliefs regarding gen-AI, including its negative effects, that any gen-AI used in any process of game development is not okay, noting specifically that "AI-generated code is not an exception to these harms," and more.

"For those reasons, this year we are declining to vote for any game that uses generative AI in any capacity," the statement says. "We urge the IGF to adopt a strong anti-AI policy for future years that disallows games containing any AI-generated work." The statement then includes the names of the IGF jurors who signed it.

Big Walk isn't specifically mentioned within that statement. However, Kyle LeClair, a four-time IGF judge and a juror for the upcoming IGF, tells Aftermath that "it got to the point where the most-discussed game this year almost entirely involved its AI usage, overshadowing pretty much everything else." LeClair says it felt like a boiling point, adding, "Anyhow, strong props to the jurors for taking this stance and putting out this letter as well, even if some people believe that using AI for coding purposes is a more gray area, we're at a point where the amount of AI slop clogging up the indie game scene means having to take hard stances such as this in order to discourage such an amount of recklessness."

Again, no mention of Big Walk. However, game developer Bruno Diaz took to BlueSky to confirm the speculation: that most-discussed game was Big Walk. "Okay, because the cat is out of the f---ing bag, I might as well combat misinformation a bit: 1. The reason IGF judges are aware of the LLM use in the development of Big Walk is through a disclosure shared by House House. 2. This disclosure was required by IGF rules. 3. While some have characterized the LLM usage as just fixing one individual blocking bug, this is a bit inaccurate; the description given by House House mentioned there being several instances, though they did also say it was mostly 'consultative' use and not code gen or agents."

Diaz notes that they believe that distinction is without a difference, adding that "to my knowledge, it is not the case that Big Walk is non-compliant with the former [Steam's AI disclosure requirements]."

"Yes, there was a large discussion about this in internal IGF forums," Diaz said. "Yes, a lot of people said things that I personally think were disingenuous, extremely disappointing, or just (frankly) dumb. No, I have no intention of talking about it in further detail or exposing anyone. [...] Ultimately, it is extremely difficult for a group of over 100 people to keep a secret so I expected this to come out eventually. Shrug emoji. If you think something is reputationally damaging, consider not doing it."

With discussion surrounding Big Walk happening during the IGF discussions, House House updated its FAQ to address, "Was AI used to make Big Walk?" Here's what the FAQ reads, in full:

"In the final stretch of Big Walk’s development, LLMs were used sparingly by House House to help work through difficult technical challenges and bugs. In some cases, snippets from LLM responses were copied as a starting point to be modified into game code—we’d estimate that well under 0.1% of Big Walk’s code had anything to do with this usage, and generative AI was not used in any other context when making the game.

The primary use case for House House’s use of LLMs was to research, via chatbots, issues we encountered with third-party code. If you’re technically-minded, and curious, here’s an example. We needed to cull shadow casters by distance from the camera, but Unity URP only allows culling shadow casters by distance in camera forwards, so shadow casters behind the player were being rendered at an infinite distance. This made our game run 50% slower for around 20 seconds at sunrise and sunset. We researched the problem extensively, and we looked at the URP code ourselves, but we couldn’t find a way. Then, we were able to speak directly to an engineer at Unity, who asked around and ultimately concluded that what we wanted wasn’t possible. Finally, we posed the question to an LLM chatbot. After a few dead ends, it suggested a possible fix, and while we had to modify the suggestion extensively, it worked. This fix represented about 10 lines of code inside URP.

We originally wrote a version of the above disclosure as it was a suggested part of our IGF submission. We have not made any disclosure on Steam as the platform does not request disclosure of code or chatbot usage. We are posting this disclosure as it has become a matter of public interest.

This is not an endorsement of, or argument for, the use of AI tools, however minimal. We have some concern that voluntary disclosures like this might contribute to the normalisation of this technology, or its treatment as “inevitable”. We support the work of those who are trying to limit the harm generative AI is doing to videogames and our world, and apologise that Big Walk’s LLM usage may not meet their standards.

Big Walk was developed without an internal AI usage policy in place, and we consider that lack of policy a failure. We will work to have a more comprehensive policy going forwards."

As you can see, House House did not disclose its use of AI-generated code because "Steam as a platform does not request disclosure of code or chatbot usage." It says it is posting the disclosure now as "it has become a matter of public interest."

House House recently made headlines for choosing not to put Big Walk on Xbox in accordance with the Palestinian-led BDS boycott against Microsoft Games. Earlier this year, it gained widespread critical acclaim for its unique emphasis on cooperative puzzle-solving – you can read more about that in Game Informer's Big Walk review.

#4182. Diablo 4's next season is short, but it lets you become The Butcher, and it has Doom: The Dark Ages skins you probably can't afford

Blizzard has unveiled the next Diablo 4 season, which kicks off next week to hold us over until the launch of the game's big expansion in April.

The big Diablo 4 Developer Update has indeed delivered the goods. One of the livestream’s big topics was, of course, the game’s upcoming mini-season, which is set to kick off next week and run until the launch of Lord of Hatred, the game’s anticipated next expansion.

You can tell Blizzard wanted to have a bit of fun with Season of Slaughter, as many of its major features make it look like a limited-time event, but there is plenty to be excited about here.

Season of Slaughter kicks off March 11, and will run until the following season kicks off April 28, with the launch of the Lord of Hatred expansion. Many of the season’s biggest additions were available to preview in the 2.6.0 Public Test Realm.

Patch 2.6.0, as you might have guessed, is the one that will kick off the slaughter next week. The headline feature here is ability to become The Butcher, the iconic in-game boss who randomly invades players’ games.

When you play as The Butcher, you’ll be rewarded the more kills you get in quick succession. Your skills hotbar will transform to become something more fitting of The Butcher, making them more brutal. You’ll also earn a seasonal currency as you play.

Starting the seasonal questline is how you can begin to assume The Butcher’s form. A Taste of Power can be initiated from Gea Kul. Transforming into The Butcher can be done in a few ways. As you play, you’ll earn Meaty Offerings, which can later be spent on Shrines of Slaughter in the new Helltide. Once activated, the shrine will draw more enemies towards you.

If you never venture into PvP zones in Diablo 4, this season may change your mind. The standard PvP combat that could only be found in Fields of Hatred has been replaced with a Ceremony of Slaughter, a new event that rewards you for killing enemies quickly. See it through and The Butcher’s Idol will spawn, allowing you to transform into it.

Elsewhere in the world, you’ll also be able to attain the same power at Slaughterhouses, a new activity type available this season. Inside, you immediately become The Butcher for the entirety of the run.

The Butcher’s arrival also ties into two of the other Season of Slaughter’s more interesting additions. First, the Killstreak system finally arrives in Diablo 4, rewarding you for being as efficient as possible in carving your way through enemies.

Anyone who played Diablo 3 should be familiar with how it works. It kicks off the moment you get a kill, and has a visible timer where you’ll need continue performing the same action to up your streak. The more kills you get, the more often your timer will refresh.

There are five tiers to climb through: Killstreak, Carnage, Devastation, Bloodbath, and Massacre. You’re awarded for the tier you manage to reach before the timer runs out. You’ll earn XP and seasonal rep each time a Killstreak is achieved.

The other Butcher-themed addition is Bloodied Items, which is a new item quality available throughout this season. They play into the Killstreak system to grant you even more power. Bloodied Items come with unique affixes that scale off your Killstreak tier. You’ll see many familiar items in that pool, as any item in the game has a chance to drop as Bloodied. Bloodied Items can also be acquired by earning Fresh Meat.

Even if none of that sounds exciting, you’re probably going to redownload the game for The Paladin free trial, which kicks off alongside the new season on March 11. The trial is only available until March 18, and it lets you try out the Paladin class.

The trial is available across PC, PlayStation, and Xbox. You’ll be able to take the new class for a spin, but your progress will be capped at level 25. The Paladin can be permanently unlocked by buying the Lord of Hatred expansion, as it’s one of two classes the expansion is introducing.

The good news is that any progress you make in the free trial will carry over to the full game if/when you buy the expansion.

Season of Slaughter also kicks off a Doom: The Dark Ages collaboration event. As we’ve come to expect, there’s a very limited free component to the collaboration, in the form of the Doom Reliquary. This is essentially a mini-battle pass that includes the Shield Saw skin, Slayer’s Flair, the head of the Cyberdemon as a back trophy and various other smaller bits.

The more impressive items - such as character skins, will instead be available to purchase for real money. The list includes the Doom Slayer armor, Mecha Dragon Serrat skin for your cat mount, and a Cacodemon pet.

Though the armor skin is cross-class compatible, judging by how much previous collaboration items have cost in Diablo 4, most of us probably won’t be spending that kind of money to get it.

#4181. XBOX CEO Casually Reveals Wolfenstein 3 In Production

Daniel is a lifelong gamer with a love for various genres and gameplay styles who enjoys exploring games and playing from various angles.

The XBOX brand, through its various acquisitions, has managed to obtain ownership of some of the oldest, arguably most important video game IPs. One of those IPs is Wolfenstein, the series that gave us the first true FPS with the release of Wolfenstein 3D all the way back in 1992. Since 2014, the Wolfenstein IP has been in the hands of MachineGames, with Bethesda serving as publisher. Microsoft owns ZeniMax, Zennimax owns Bethesda, and so XBOX usually gets first dibs when Wolfenstein comes knocking.

You might not think it, but a serious shooter like Wolfenstein 3D was a huge influence, according to Randy Pitchford.

It’s rather fitting, then, that someone high up the chain of command in XBOX would have the privilege of divulging new Wolfenstein news. Though, even then, I certainly wouldn’t expect the someone in question to be its literal CEO, nor would I expect said news to drop on a random Thursday, but let nobody say they can’t make things interesting.

On her personal X, formerly Twitter account, XBOX CEO Asha Sharma rather casually announced that MachineGames has officially begun production on the next mainline Wolfenstein game, the first since Wolfenstein II: The New Colossus was released in 2017. Obviously, since production has just started, details are basically non-existent, but both Sharma and MachineGames’ own X account did give us a couple of tidbits to chew on.

Sharma’s tweet keeps the announcement fairly quick and concise, reading, “Wolfenstein 3 is officially in production at @MachineGames. One of gaming's most important franchises, and a team that has done remarkable work bringing it forward. Looking forward to sharing more.”

One of gaming's most important franchises, and a team that has done remarkable work bringing it forward.

Assuming the game will have some manner of subtitle like its predecessors, Sharma didn’t divulge what it was. What she did share, though, was a screenshot of the game’s apparent script. This screenshot is apparently set during the game’s first chapter in a locale called “Nazitraz,” presumably a prison of some sort, in which series protagonist B.J. Blazkowicz confronts a man named “Otto,” who blubbers in fear in his presence. Series mainstay Fergus Reid also appears to be present, but the screenshot cuts off before he says or does anything.

The Elder Scrolls 6 has finally had its title officially confirmed, weeks after it was not so subtly leaked to the wider public.

Shortly after Sharma’s tweet, MachineGames shared the same script screenshot on its own X account alongside the caption, “His reputation precedes him. Wolfenstein 3 is in production.” MachineGames’ post also added a photo of two actors in the midst of motion-capture work: Debra Wilson, who previously played Grace Walker in New Colossus, and B.J.’s actor, Brian Bloom.

Wolfenstein, as a series, has been pretty quiet for a few years now. As I mentioned, New Colossus was the last mainline game to release, which was nearly a decade ago in 2017. The series has had spin-offs since then, including Wolfenstein: Youngblood and Wolfenstein: Cyberpilot, both of which were released in 2019. The former was a co-op game starring B.J.’s teenage daughters as they searched for their father in France, while the latter was a VR game in which an unnamed hacker works to hack various Nazi robots. Unfortunately, neither of these games were particularly well-received.

Still, there’s no reason to be pessimistic, especially considering that it was MachineGames that brought us the unexpected slam dunk that was Indiana Jones and the Great Circle in 2024. I’d say that’s pretty definitive proof that the studio still knows how to put an excellent game together, and I’m optimistic about what’s on the horizon.

Incidentally, MachineGames is also involved in a creative capacity for the live-action Wolfenstein series that’s currently in development for Prime Video. Who knows, we might just have a one-two punch of new Wolfenstein media to look forward to in the not-too-distant future.

MachineGames is making sure the Indiana Jones DLC is challenging, no matter how many hours you've put into the base game.

#4180. Xbox CEO Announces A New Id Software Doom Game Is In The Works

Ever since Doom: The Dark Ages was released, ID Software has been under intense pressure from Xbox regarding its lengthy development time and high financial expectations. Despite some pretty harsh treatment towards the creatives behind the new Doom games, however, it seems Xbox is placing some large bets on the studio by officially announcing both a new game and a free update for The Dark Ages.

Shared by none other than Xbox CEO Asha Sharma herself on X, the post started by saying that the new 'Slaughter Mode,' similar to Doom Eternal's Horde game mode, would be arriving early next week, followed by the confirmation that the studio is already "working on its next game."

While we've known about the existence of a new Doom game since July, this is the first official confirmation that Id Software is in fact still heading the franchise with an exciting new entry despite the brutal layoffs the studio experienced over the summer as a result of Microsoft's downsizing.

Coming far sooner in comparison, the free Slaughter Mode update for Doom: The Dark Ages, releasing on November 16, will offer a roguelike-style game mode where each run is randomized for additional replayability and challenges, as shown in the official trailer shared by Bethesda Softworks on YouTube.

With a total of 19 arenas to play through from both The Dark Ages and its Revelation expansion, you'll be able to exchange points from completing challenges and weekly rewards for cosmetics like skins, backgrounds, soundtracks, and more. Checkpoints will also offer the chance to ramp up the difficulty in exchange for greater rewards, albeit at a much higher risk of losing all your progress if you fail.

While the mode is a welcome addition for fans of the Doom reboots itching for an excuse to revisit its satisfyingly brutal gameplay loop, the update and praise for the new game headed by Id Software's Texas and Frankfurt teams alongside the help of Hugo Martin has left a sour taste in some players' mouths.

An anonymous id Software developer has spoken out against Xbox, "They have destroyed immense amounts of value."

Despite responding to the post with excitement over the project, several leaks from insiders within the studio have reported that things are still shaky within the studio, which has now been reduced to roughly the same size as its Doom (2016) development team.

Even though the studio has more than proven its abilities over the years, hopefully the additional praise from Xbox comes with a bit more support for the studio responsible for some of gaming's most iconic shooters.

#4179. Pikmin 4 Is Still Great, But Dandori Academy Is Underwhelming

Pikmin 4 was released for the original Switch in 2023, and it ranks among my favorite games on the platform; I happily award it the honor of being the best Pikmin game. It looks and plays great, and Oatchi the dog makes the sometimes annoying process of managing a collection of little plant creatures willing to do your bidding much smoother.

The over-titled Pikmin 4 – Nintendo Switch 2 Edition + Dandori Academy releases November 12, and much like other comparable Nintendo games that have been ported and improved for Switch 2 (like Kirby and Mario Party), the base game is as good as it was initially and looks even better. If you skipped Pikmin 4 on Switch for whatever reason (probably because it was day one of the Barbenheimer epidemic), I encourage you to play it now. You have about a week to beat it before… something else comes out. Who’s to say.

The “big” addition here for the Switch 2 version of the game, alongside improved performance and visuals and the ability to give Oatchi verbal commands, is Dandori Academy. The Academy is an expanded time trial mode that awards medals for practicing specific levels, which you can then play and upload your high scores on specific days. For example, I can play the Advanced B level, Rockaway Cellars, as much as I want, but it only really counts if I play it on November 12. And you only get one try (though you can unlock retry tickets).

In theory, I like the unique approach to high-score battling, and the limited timeframe adds fun intensity, but this isn't what I am looking for from Pikmin. I recognize and acknowledge the design decision to place timers on your interactions in Pikmin, but it’s never been my favorite part. I like building my adorable little army and exploring, discovering, and retrieving as many unexpected items as possible. But I mostly get annoyed at the ticking clock, especially when I am watching my crew meander toward my spaceship holding a Game Boy Advance SP (or whatever they manage to find on the never-acknowledged, but potentially post-apocalyptic Earth you are exploring).

I also like having a list of missions to complete, and in Dandori Academy, there isn’t much acknowledgment of your success in practice. You can earn a platinum medal while practicing Rockaway Cellar, but it’s mainly to let you know that this is what you could earn when you play on the right day.

The main takeaway is that Pikmin 4 is still excellent, and I was grateful to transfer my save file from the Switch version (and I was tempted to start a new game + save), but Dandori Academy is not a strong incentive to return if you already played the game. It is a nice bonus and an interesting concept that reimagines the familiar time trial mode featured in plenty of video games, but the original campaign is still the main attraction.

#4178. Diablo 4’s Warlock looks like an unhinged Necromancer with Sorcerer energy in first look at gameplay

Diablo 4's practitioner of forbidden arts, The Warlock, has been officially unveiled as the second class coming with Lord of Hatred.

Thanks to a meaty, well-produced Diablo 4 Developer Update, we got to have our promised first look at gameplay of the Warlock, the second of two classes coming to the game with the upcoming Lord of Hatred expansion.

The showcase offered a deep look at the Warlock’s core archetypes, its gameplay and skills loop, and where the class sits within the game’s existing roster of diverse classes.

Since the initial reveal of Lord of Hatred, The Warlock has remained the mysterious second class. Anyone who pre-purchased the expansion was able to get immediate access to The Paladin, the other class arriving with the expansion. It wasn’t until February that Blizzard officially revealed the class to the world, but we had to wait until this most recent Developer Update to actually see it in action.

The Warlock’s pragmatism exists as the counterpart to The Paladin's purity, in that Warlocks don’t shy away from harnessing the powers of Hell to eliminate their enemies. The class can conjure up demons to do their bidding, and utilise attacks previously only available to legions of Hell.

The Warlock is a hybrid pet and caster class. Their gameplay revolves around summoning demons, and undermining enemies with shadow arts. They rely on two resources: Wrath, and Dominance. Casting Skills consumes Wrath, whereas Dominance is what allows the Warlock to summon and exploit demons.

The Warlock has four archetypes players can spec into. Legions are traditional summoners who rely on overwhelming numbers to crush enemies. Vanguards are closer to Sorcerers, capable of dealing damage head-on. Masterminds utilise shadowcraft to slowly drain their enemies. Finally, Ritualists are summoners of the most terrifying Hell demons.

The Warlock is able to do this by fusing Soul Shards into their bodies. Going down any of the four paths becomes available after reaching level 30, which is when the class mechanic is unlocked. Each Soul Shard is tied to a certain demon, and its through that power that the Warlock is able to call upon them in combat. Your choice does, of course, affect your abilities going forward.

Warlocks arrive alongside new Uniques that cater to their specific playstyles, which is similar to what we’ve previously seen with The Paladin, and The Spiritborn before that.

Lord of Hatred arrives April 28. While we wait, Diablo 4’s next season is kicking off next week to deliver a bit of mindless fun to hold us over until the big day.

#4177. Marvel Cosmic Invasion's Doctor Doom-Themed DLC Gives It The Post-Game Tail It Was Missing

Marvel Cosmic Invasion was a bit of a dream game for me; I loved the X-Men arcade game in the '90s, so when Tribute Games released the excellent Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles: Shredder's Revenge in 2022, I immediately hoped they'd revitalize other licensed brawler franchises released by Konami in the late '80s and early '90s. While we still haven't heard any word of a new brawler starring The Simpsons, Tribute did follow up its Turtle triumph with Marvel Cosmic Invasion, another throwback side-scrolling beat 'em up, this time starring Marvel's mightiest.

I played through Marvel Cosmic Invasion multiple times and had a blast, but I moved on quickly, as I didn't feel the need to collect different palette-swaps of the many heroes on offer. Even after Cyclops and The Thing joined the roster as DLC in May, I still saw Cosmic Invasion as a game in the rearview. That changes this week, as The Siege of Castle Doom not only adds two additional playable characters (Invisible Woman and Doctor Doom), but also a mode that has the potential to bring me back for more runs for the foreseeable future.

Seeing that Annihilus is threatening the universe, Doom decides to take matters into his own hands. Unfortunately, much in the way that it seems that he may try to fix the multiversal incursions in the upcoming Avengers: Doomsday, Victor Von Doom's solution in Marvel Cosmic Invasion – the Cosmic Inductor – would lead to untold death and destruction. In The Siege of Castle Doom, you select your team and fight your way through various floors of the stronghold belonging to the man who is perhaps Marvel's greatest villain. Your goal is to fight through the winding, randomized hallways of Castle Doomstadt, charging Reed Richards' Stabilizer and tactically bolstering your team along the way, before Doctor Doom can enact his plan.

As for the new playable characters, Doctor Doom is less agile, but his attacks pack a whallop, while Invisible Woman's force fields and speed make her the more versatile pick. I don't know that I see either of them replacing my mains from the base game, but I had fun experimenting with them throughout this mode. Regardless of which character you choose from the expanding roster, you still must traverse Castle Doomstadt before Doom achieves his objective.

Fighting through waves of enemies across differently themed and booby-trapped rooms, you encounter all manner of foes from the base game, as well as new minion types from Doom. When you defeat enemies, they drop batteries that charge your Stabilizer, letting you even the odds and stop Doom. Conversely, each time an enemy hits your character, it charges Doom's Cosmic Inductor, inching him closer to victory and making his minions faster and stronger in the process. As you might expect, the rooms get harder the deeper you go, and while each player starts with two characters to swap between, if a character completely depletes their health, they're gone for good, making it even tougher. As such, you need to keep your eyes on each character's health and swap them out when it makes sense.

As you complete each room, you can choose which path to take to augment your characters with new special abilities. True to the roguelite structure, as you complete rooms, you can also buff your characters' stats within the run. Certain rooms offer extra batteries to help your Stabilizer charge, while others offer new and upgraded equipment. There's also one that promises random events that can easily alter the trajectory of your run for better or worse. Though I often enjoyed boosting attack stats to make enemies less like damage sponges, I had to balance that against buffing their health to keep them alive and charging the Stabilizer to have a fighting chance.

Beyond the in-run upgrades and modifiers, you can also amp up the action run-over-run through upgrades in Reed's Lab, which add to the pool of modifiers you can select from at the start of each run. The expansion also adds new palettes for existing heroes, plus new music by composer Tee Lopes. While I've only done a few runs of The Siege of Castle Doom (each taking between 45 and 90 minutes, depending on how successful you are), I feel a revitalized sense of excitement for Marvel Cosmic Invasion. Tribute claims completionists can spend upwards of 15 hours in this new mode, which has me champing at the bit to dive back into what will likely be my primary way of interacting with Marvel Cosmic Invasion going forward.

Marvel Cosmic Invasion – The Siege of Castle Doom is available today on all platforms, and it is a strong addition to an already great game. You can read our review of the base version of Marvel Cosmic Invasion here.

#4176. Valve Leak Shows Off Assets For Half-Life 3 And Cancelled MMO

Half-Life 3 has long since grown to mythological proportions over the years, with countless rumors and gaming events hyped as the first-ever reveal for the new title. While most of these leaks and rumors have rarely ever amounted to anything, the past few months have seen more than their fair share of credible reveals for the third entry in the dystopian sci-fi series thanks to the 12TB Steam leak.

While there's still no telling when we'll actually get to see Half-Life 3's existence officially acknowledged by Valve, some users have recently discovered even more assets from an ancient build of the original Half-Life 2: Episode 3.

Although several Steam news accounts like Gabe Follower were quick to share the discovery, one of the clearest photos was posted by Scolcer on X, allowing fans to see the sheer scale of the environments that would have been in store for players if the 2013 build of Half-Life 2 Episode 3 had ever been released.

While there was some confusion over what assets included in the recent discovery were actually from Half-Life 3 or Valve's canceled sci-fi MMO Stars of Blood, especially given the Combine-like design of the ship included in the map, fans have managed to narrow it down to the spacecraft designs being from Stars of Blood, while the map itself is almost certainly from the unreleased Half-Life 2: Episode 3.

As if the massive mechanical pillars from Half-Life weren't enough of a clue, the snowy map matches up perfectly with the concept art and early asset reveals from the canceled Half-Life 2: Episode 3, which would have seen Gordon and Alyx traveling to the Arctic to investigate the dilapidated Borealis research facility.

After waiting so long for Half-Life 3, it'd be a crime if it ended on another cliffhanger.

While we'll likely never get to see this version of Half-Life realized, that doesn't mean the project has been canceled just yet, as several rumors and even a recent leak by a Valve employee suggest that some form of Half-Life 3 is still in development under the codename Half-Life X.

Even though it's unlikely, the heavily rumored project could wind up reusing similar concepts like the ones fans are still discovering to this day from Half-Life 3's 2013 build, well over a decade after its predecessor's.

#4175. Reminder: The Final Kirby Air Riders amiibo Are Now Available

Since the arrival of Kirby Air Riders on the Switch 2 last year, Nintendo has been releasing amiibo for the game on a regular basis.

In case you missed the previous updates, this week marks the arrival of the "final figures" in this series. It's Sword Kirby & Dragoon, and Noir Dedede & Hyrda. This particular line allows you to swap the riders and machines around. Here's a little more about what else they do:

"Tap this amiibo featuring in Kirby Air Riders to summon Figure Players in-game that you can train and level up. You can even swap riders just like in the game to choose your rider and machine."

They'll set you back $54.99 / £41.99 each (or your regional equivalent) and can be purchased on the Nintendo Store and from retailers online and in-store. There are a total of seven Kirby Air Riders amiibo to collect.

This follows a game update for Kirby Air Riders last week, which included some bug fixes. The update before this in June (Version 1.3.3) made these latest amiibo figures compatible.

#4174. Marathon launch player numbers are about half those of the Server Slam, at least on PC

Marathon hasn't quite been able to attract the same volume of players the recent Server Slam did.

After a couple of delays, a plagiarism lawsuit, and at least one internal reboot, Bungie’s next big game has officially launched. Marathon, the extraction shooter from the studio behind Destiny, has managed to find a decent, if a little small of an audience.

The game’s player numbers on Steam are being compared to its recent free, open weekend, and not in a favourable manner.

Prior to Marathon’s launch, Bungie held a multi-day Server Slam, which offered anyone interested in playing the game a chance to try out almost all of its classes, two of its maps, as well as many of its gameplay and progression systems.

The open test was largely well-received, and players actually showed up for it. It peaked at a very respectable 143,621 concurrent players on Steam, which put it within striking distance of the peak concurrent of its chief competitor, Arc Raiders - at least when you compare both of their pre-launch Server Slam events.

In Arc Raiders’ case, those figures were far outpaced at the game’s actual launch, and the Embark shooter continues to command a very active player base to this day. A paid product garnering far more players than the same product’s own free sampler is never not a good sign, so many hoped something similar would happen with Marathon.

Marathon has now officially launched, and it doesn’t look like it managed to pull an Arc Raiders - at least so far. At its peak, the Bungie shooter attracted 88,337 concurrent players on Steam (via SteamDB), which is a little over half of its Server Slam’s 143,621 peak concurrent.

Numbers have, of course, dropped since then, which is normal, as players log off for the night. This is obviously not the end of the road for Marathon. Friday, and the weekend, may well push numbers closer to the Server Slam heights.

Indeed, word of mouth is quite positive, with the game currently sitting at a Very Positive user review rating on Steam, based on over 4,600 reviews. As has been proven time and time again in recent years, nothing catapults a game like players emphatically advocating for it to their friends, so it could simply be that mainstream players are cautious.

It will become clear where things settle over the weekend.

#4173. Marathon’s Symbiosis Update Adds Host Of New Modes, Including Permanent PvE, Next Month

Bungie has detailed its upcoming Symbiosis update for Marathon, which introduces several significant modes next month. Chief among them is the new permanent PvE mode, which Bungie previously experimented with and promised earlier this year.

Symbiosis is headlined by Expedition, a co-op PvE destination with roguelite elements. Expedition pits teams of players against escalating challenges and offers randomized upgrades called Flash Boosts to increase their odds of success.

The Perimeter zone has also been expanded with the new Burrows and Reservoir areas. Another addition is Limbo, a new social hub for players to gather that features a firing range. You can also try out the new sword-wielding Bishop Runner Shell alongside new weapons and gear, such as the Maverick pistol, throwing knife, hack grenade, and V17 flamethrower. Lastly, you can test your skills against other players in the beta PvP Deathmatch mode.

Symbiosis arrives in Marathon on December 8. An open play week will kick off the same day, allowing new players to experience all of Marathon’s content for free until December 15.

The Symbiosis update marks Marathon's evolution into a more co-op-friendly, PvE experience as its initial focus on PvP extraction has struggled to sustain a substantial audience since its March 5 launch. Bungie announced in September that it plans to spend the rest of 2026 improving Marathon's core mechanics and features while giving players more agency for how they engage with it beyond competitive PvP.

For more on Marathon, check out our review.

#4172. Xbox Vs. PS5: GTA 6 Specs Revealed, And These Are The Biggest Differences

"Pushing both platforms to their absolute limits"

Rockstar Games has today lifted the lid on a bunch of specs for both the Xbox and PS5 versions of GTA 6, revealing some of the biggest differences (and similarities) between playing the game on each platform.

The most notable bit of information is that every single console runs the game at 30FPS. Regardless of whether you're playing on Xbox Series S, Xbox Series X, PS5 or even PS5 Pro, the max you're getting is 30 frames per-second.

"Grand Theft Auto VI has been fully developed from the ground up to provide the best possible experience for the current generation of consoles, targeting 30 frames per second while pushing both platforms to their absolute limits to bring the vast and rich world of Leonida to life — while maintaining the density and visual fidelity of all its environments and inhabitants."

There will obviously be resolution differences between each platform, but Rockstar has yet to reveal these details. Expect the Series S to fare the worst, the PS5 Pro to fare the best, and the Series X and PS5 to be pretty much equal.

Rockstar does say that GTA 6 "plays best" on PS5 though (and let's not forget that Sony appears to have a marketing deal in place with Rockstar Games for this release), highlighting the differences between the PS5 and Xbox versions as being "high-fidelity haptic feedback" for the PS5 DualSense controllers, improved spatial audio rendering, and bizarrely, improved load times. That last one is surely just a minimal advantage at best!

Grand Theft Auto VI for PS5 includes high-fidelity haptic feedback fully integrated across the game on DualSense controllers and adjustable via accessibility settings, improved spatial audio rendering so all in-game sounds take full advantage of Tempest 3D Audio, and improved load times, making Grand Theft Auto VI play best on PlayStation 5 consoles.

Beyond that, the PS5 Pro version will benefit from improved clarity via PSSR along with ray-traced shadows.

However, the Xbox version has one massive benefit in the form of Xbox Cloud Gaming. It seems Xbox will be the only platform offering cloud streaming for GTA 6 at launch, making it an exclusive of sorts - at least for now. The bizarre bit is that it only appears to be for consoles, rather than other devices like PCs and mobiles.

The Xbox and PS5 versions will also support Remote Play (allowing you to cast your game to another device from your console). Nothing has been said about Quick Resume yet on Xbox, but we assume it'll be supported as well.

Ultimately, GTA 6 is bound to run great regardless of whether you buy it on Xbox or PlayStation, and the "plays best on PS5" differences mentioned by Rockstar Games appear to be minor advantages rather than major ones.

We can't wait for footage to start appearing online next week — especially for the Xbox Series S version — and here's hoping it's going to live up to the ridiculous hype that's been fueling the past decade. Not long to wait at all now!

Beyond corporate culture, I'm not naive either. I also believe Microsoft is subject to much stricter scrutiny from competition regulators than Sony because it's a Big Tech company. Take Crunchyroll as an example. In my opinion, that acquisition should never have been approved. Sony ended up controlling the overwhelming majority of the anime-focused streaming market in both the United States and Europe. That should never have been allowed to happen. Sony is also the world's largest music publisher through its acquisition of numerous music catalogs, and critics argue that its licensing practices have contributed to higher costs for streaming platforms and, ultimately, consumers. That's part of the company's culture, in my view. Sony often seems willing to push as far as possible, even when it results in higher costs for consumers.
